Hi Jane — thanks for the heads-up and the scope doc. Looping in Laura (sales) and Karthik (legal) + Monica (security/ops) to confirm details below.

Short answers up front:
- Standard pen-test notice: we typically request 14 days' notice for scheduled vendor-led tests. For internal/emergency incident-driven tests we can accept 48 hours' notice with a post-test evidence packet.
- Evidence cadence: Redwood provides SOC2 Type II annual reports on request (we can include certificate + report in the order form exhibit), monthly vulnerability scan summaries, and a weekly access-logs export by default for dedicated customers. For hosted customers we provide a monthly logs export and on-demand extracts for audits.

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal to confirm acceptable notice language for the MSA/security exhibit (Karthik)
2) Ops to own the evidence cadence table and map each artifact to an owner and format (Monica)
3) I'll send a redlined security exhibit for MediSys that includes the proposed notice window and the evidence cadence summary.

Attaching our working security exhibit for your review: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v3.docx

Vivek / Jane — quick legal read:

1) Notice period: Karthik (legal) suggests we standardize on a 14-day notice for scheduled third-party pen tests in the Security Exhibit, with an explicit carve-out allowing for incident-driven or regulator-ordered tests with 48 hours' notice and documentation afterwards. That balances customer operational needs and Redwood's ability to coordinate back-end changes.

2) Audit rights / scope: we will keep the audit rights narrow — access for the purposes of compliance verification only, no full-source access, and any on-site requests must be pre-authorized. We should include a requirement for a mutually-agreed scope and a limit on frequency (e.g., up to 2 vendor-conducted pen tests per 12 months unless both parties agree to more).

3) Evidence delivery: require Redwood to provide the SOC2 report annually on request and to provide logs/vulnerability artifacts on a monthly or as-requested basis. We should avoid open-ended continuous exports unless covered in Dedicated contracts.

I'll prepare redline diffs to the security exhibit with suggested MSA language and a short glide path for evidence cadence. Sending security-exhibit-redline-diff.docx to the thread.

--

- Notice window: our preference for third-party tests is 30 days to coordinate vendor booking and change control. - Frequency: 2 vendor tests per year is acceptable; we might request an additional test on a pay-per-test basis.
